sources.title: Mars Fact Sheet
sources.values_read: Surface gravity (mean) 3.73 m/s²; surface acceleration 3.69 (equator), 3.73 (pole) m/s²; solar irradiance 586.2 W/m²; sidereal rotation period 24.6229 h; length of day 24.6597 h; surface pressure 6.36 mb at mean radius, varying from 4.0 to 8.7 mb with season; average temperature about 214 K (−59 °C); atmosphere CO2 95.1%, N2 2.59%, Ar 1.94%, O2 0.16%, CO 0.06% by volume.
sources.supports: TS-03 gravity. Planet facts in the source screen. Not electrical panel output and not local weather.
sources.mission_site: Whole planet (global values, not one site)
sources.units: m/s², W/m², h, mb, K, °C, % by volume
sources.note: Page says "Last Updated: 19 May 2025". Evidence: Reference values compiled by NASA; global, not site-specific

sources.title: Mars24 Sunclock — Technical Notes on Mars Solar Time
sources.values_read: Mean solar day (sol): 24 h 39 min 35.244 s. Sidereal day: 24 h 37 min 22.663 s. (88,775.244 s is arithmetic from the first figure; the page gives no seconds-only value.)
sources.supports: TS-01: explains that the 20-minute sol is a game-time control, not the length of a Martian day.
sources.note: "(Updated 2023-05-15)". Evidence: Reference value

sources.title: Rover Environmental Monitoring Station Data
sources.kind: Document that links to the archive at https://atmos.nmsu.edu/PDS/data/PDS4/msl_rems_bundle/
sources.values_read: Quantities archived: wind speed and direction, pressure, relative humidity, air temperature, ground temperature, ultraviolet radiation. Coverage text: 7 Aug 2012 (sol 1) to 22 March 2025 (sol 4488), marked ongoing; the volume links are labelled sols 1–4843.
sources.supports: WX-01, WX-02. Gaps: data set identifiers are not printed on the page; landing site is not named on the page; the two coverage figures disagree (C-16); no product was downloaded.
sources.mission_site: Curiosity rover, REMS weather station; Gale crater (named in the register, not on the page)
sources.observation_dates: 7 Aug 2012 (sol 1) to 22 March 2025 (sol 4488), marked ongoing; the volume links are labelled sols 1–4843
sources.note: Evidence: Measured Mars data

sources.title: MEDA - Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer
sources.kind: Document that links to the bundle at https://atmos.nmsu.edu/PDS/data/PDS4/Mars2020/mars2020_meda/
sources.values_read: DOI 10.17189/1522849. Levels: raw, partially processed, calibrated, derived, SkyCam. Calibrated quantities: pressure, humidity, wind, temperatures, radiation. Coverage from 19 Feb 2021, marked ongoing. Collection sizes listed: calibrated 10 GB, derived 2.9 GB.
sources.supports: WX-01, WX-02. Gaps: no urn:nasa:pds identifier on the page; no product downloaded; dust opacity product not identified.
sources.mission_site: Perseverance rover, MEDA weather station; Jezero crater (named in the register, not on the page)
sources.note: Evidence: Measured and derived Mars data

sources.title: Insight Archive Page
sources.supports: Optional third site. Gap: site name not on the page.
sources.mission_site: InSight lander, TWINS and pressure sensor; site name not on the page
sources.note: Evidence: Measured Mars data

sources.title: News releases on InSight power and dust
sources.values_read: Leads: about 5,000 Wh per sol after landing, about 500 by spring 2022; a regional storm cut 425 to 275 Wh per sol.
sources.supports: Solar dust teaching event (Prompts 07, 09). Open the pages before citing. No dust optical depth value was found.
sources.note: Evidence: Measured spacecraft telemetry reported in a release

sources.title: Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS)
sources.values_read: The oxygen generation assembly electrolyzes water supplied by the Water Recovery System into oxygen and hydrogen. Carbon dioxide is removed from cabin air with molecular sieves. The page puts water recovery at about 90 percent.
sources.supports: OX-01 (electrolysis path; CO2 removal as a separate function), water recycling. ISS evidence, not Mars evidence.
sources.note: "Page Last Updated: Apr 04, 2025". Evidence: ISS analog

sources.title: NASA's Oxygen-Generating Experiment MOXIE Completes Mars Mission
sources.values_read: Total oxygen produced: 122 g over 16 runs. Best rate: 12 g per hour. Purity: 98% or better. Feedstock: carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere, one oxygen atom taken from each molecule.
sources.supports: OX-01 (atmospheric CO2 path), OX-02 (label the fictional scale-up).
sources.note: Evidence: Technology demonstration on Mars, small scale

sources.title: MOXIE results paper (title, authors and year not read)
sources.values_read: Nothing. Title, authors and year are not asserted.
sources.supports: Do not cite until opened.

sources.title: ISS ECLSS overview
sources.values_read: Lead: CDRA is a four-bed molecular sieve; Sabatier closes the loop only partly.
sources.supports: Detail for the life-support explanations.
sources.note: Evidence: ISS analog

sources.title: Growing Plants in Space
sources.values_read: Crops listed as grown in Veggie: three types of lettuce, Chinese cabbage, mizuna mustard, red Russian kale, zinnia flowers. The Advanced Plant Habitat is described as a second growth chamber for plant research. Tomatoes and peppers are named as produce the Kennedy team hopes to plant in future.
sources.supports: Lettuce as a supported crop. This page does not say tomatoes were grown in Veggie; it lists them as a future plan.
sources.mission_site: International Space Station (ISS): Veggie and the Advanced Plant Habitat
sources.note: "Page Last Updated: Dec 08, 2023". Evidence: ISS analog

sources.supports: Tomato. Needs a results source, not a plan.

sources.title: MSL: CheMin (Chemistry and Mineralogy)
sources.kind: Document that links to data sets msl-m-chemin-2-edr-v1 and msl-m-chemin-4-rdr-v1
sources.values_read: CheMin measures mineral abundance by X-ray diffraction of powdered rock and soil. Latest notice on the page: MSL Release 42, 3 August 2026, adding raw and derived data for sols 4710–4843.
sources.supports: Field-sample to lab-comparison activity (Prompt 08). Gap: no specific sample product chosen. A Gale sample is not a measurement of the fictional map.
sources.mission_site: Curiosity rover (MSL), CheMin instrument; Gale crater
sources.note: Evidence: Measured and derived Mars data (Gale crater)

sources.title: MSL: SAM (Sample Analysis at Mars)
sources.kind: Document that links to data sets
sources.values_read: Processing levels 0, 1A, 1B and 2. The page notes that raw SAM products are stored safely but are not formally archived in PDS.
sources.supports: Alternative sample source.
sources.note: Evidence: Measured and derived Mars data

sources.title: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle
sources.values_read: Mass 210 kg, payload 490 kg, two 36 V silver-zinc batteries of 121 Ah, crew of two.
sources.supports: Explaining mass, payload, battery range and traction trade-offs. A two-seat lunar vehicle, not a four-seat Mars rover.
sources.note: Evidence: Lunar hardware; analog only

sources.title: NASA-STD-3001 technical brief on surface transport vehicles
sources.supports: Seating and crew-safety context.

sources.title: Earth–Mars signal delay pages
sources.values_read: Ranges differ by page: 4 to 20 minutes; 4 to 21 minutes; about 22 minutes maximum (C-18).
sources.supports: CM-02: Earth–Mars light time is separate from the fictional radio delay and from network jitter.
sources.note: One attempt to find the range on https://science.nasa.gov/mars/facts/ found only Sun–Mars light time. Evidence: Reference value

sources.values_read: Both exist. SpringArm3D is a raycast that pulls its children toward the collision point.

sources.title: Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document
sources.values_read: Table 3-31 (82 kg reference crew member, respiratory quotient 0.86, daily exercise): oxygen consumed 0.895 kg/CM-d; carbon dioxide load 1.085 kg/CM-d; food solids 0.800 kg/CM-d; food energy 12.778 MJ/CM-d; potable water 3.217 kg/CM-d; water in food 0.760; metabolic water 0.490; respiration and perspiration water 2.946; urine water 1.420; fecal water 0.101 kg/CM-d. Notes to Table 3-31: 1.56 kg/CM-d of food eaten at 48.7 % water. Table 4-20, Early Planetary Base: drinking 2.00, food rehydration 0.50, urinal flush 0.50, personal hygiene 0.4, hand wash 1.08, total water consumption 4.48 kg/CM-d; ISS column total 3.20. Table 4-21, ISS: total wastewater 3.77 kg/CM-d. Table 3-2: ISS average ECLSS power 5.31 kW. Table 3-17: lithium-ion (liquid electrolyte) 100 to 150 Wh/kg, 1,500 cycles at 60 % depth of discharge. Table 4-91: lettuce 7.78 g O2 produced and 10.70 g CO2 taken up per m² per day. Section 4.3.3: ISS urine processor recovers about 85 % of urine water (US segment).
sources.supports: GameBalance crew rates (oxygen, CO2, water, food energy per meal), wastewater share, battery sizing for scale, life-support power cross-check, Garden dome plant oxygen.
sources.section: 11. Crew use, night energy and life-support power (energy and NASA worker, 2026-11-14)
sources.note: (PDF downloaded from NTRS and read). Evidence: NASA design reference values (ISS analog and planning values; not measured on Mars)
